item.title: Jone Wesele named new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula coach
item.description: Jone Wesele has been named the new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula Coach this afternoon. Fiji National Rugby League Chair Rajesh Singh says Wesele will be assisted by Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter, Shane Morris and Joe Rabele.
item.content:encoded:
Jone Wesele has been named the new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula Coach this afternoon.

Fiji National Rugby League Chair Rajesh Singh says Wesele will be assisted by Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter, Shane Morris and Joe Rabele.

Wesele says it is extremely humbling to take on the role.

He says his immediate priority is the announcement of the 40-member squad for the Women's Rugby League World Cup in Australia in October.

The new coach says his immediate focus will also be on connecting with the coaching staff and players.

The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula will be making their Rugby League World Cup debut and are pooled with New Zealand, France and Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Shankar to lead Fiji at OFC U19 Men’s Championship
item.description: Delon Shankar has been named captain of the Fiji side for the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 in Samoa. Shankar says he is honoured and proud to lead the national side and is grateful to the officials and coaches for trusting him with the responsibility.
item.content:encoded:
Delon Shankar has been named captain of the Fiji side for the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 in Samoa.

Shankar says he is honoured and proud to lead the national side and is grateful to the officials and coaches for trusting him with the responsibility.

The young defender says he is ready to lead the side to victory and hopes to make Fiji and their families proud.

The OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 will be held in Samoa from next Tuesday to 14th September.

Defending champions New Zealand have been drawn alongside Tahiti, Fiji and Vanuatu in Group B, while hosts Samoa are joined by 2024 runners-up New Caledonia, Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea in Group A.

Fiji will face Vanuatu next Wednesday at 12pm in their opening pool match before taking on New Zealand next Saturday at 4pm.

Their final pool match will be against Tahiti on 8th September at 12pm at the Samoa Football HQ.

The winner and runner-up will qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Age no barrier for potential Flying Fijians debutant Ravuiwasa
item.description: Age is nothing but a number, and Taveuni rep Inoke Ravuiwasa is a testament to that. The 30-year-old could make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians at th e Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup next month.
item.content:encoded:
Age is nothing but a number, and Taveuni rep Inoke Ravuiwasa is a testament to that.

The 30-year-old could make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians at th e Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup next month.

Ravuiwasa has come through the domestic rugby scene, bringing significant experience from Fiji’s provincial rugby, Fiji Police rugby, the Fijian Warriors and Australia’s John I Dent Cup.

Having recently signed with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua development squad, Ravuiwasa says he always reminds himself that nothing is impossible.

He was part of the Flying Fijians squad training at the High Performance Unit gym in Laucala this morning.

The Flying Fijians will play Japan on 12th September.

item.title: Former Fijiana Mere Moto helps shape next generation of women rugby players
item.description: Former Fijiana XV player and Suva Women's rugby team Strength and Conditioning Coach Mere Moto has reflected on her decade-long rugby journey, which came full circle when she finally received her official Test cap at the same stadium where she made her international debut earlier this month. Moto made her Fijiana debut against Papua New Guinea at the then ANZ Stadium 10 years ago.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fijiana XV player and Suva Women's rugby team Strength and Conditioning Coach Mere Moto has reflected on her decade-long rugby journey, which came full circle when she finally received her official Test cap at the same stadium where she made her international debut earlier this month.

Moto made her Fijiana debut against Papua New Guinea at the then ANZ Stadium 10 years ago.

A decade later, she returned to the same venue, now HFC Bank Stadium, where she finally received her official Test cap.

Speaking on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Moto says her journey in rugby has been nothing short of amazing.

She says moving from being a player to becoming a strength and conditioning coach has allowed her to remain involved in the sport she loves while contributing in a different way.

Her interest in strength and conditioning was also influenced by her experience playing with a women’s rugby club in Australia, where one coach had to take on several roles, including coaching, strength and conditioning and management.

She enrolled in a Certificate and Trade Diploma in Sports Science at Fiji National University before gaining her World Rugby accreditation as a Strength and Conditioning Coach and later becoming a World Rugby Educator.

She says she never expected rugby to become something she would remain involved in for the rest of her life.

Today, she is continuing to contribute to women’s rugby through her work with Suva Women’s Rugby, using the experience she gained as a player and coach to help shape the next generation.

Moto is also the host of LegendFM Quiet Storm show from 7pm to midnight.

item.title: Nasova and Tuitubou extend Fijian Drua stay through 2028
item.description: Explosive backs Joji Nasova and Maika Tuitubou have extended their stay at the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua through to the 2028 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season. The duo stepped up to the competition level in 2026 after taking different pathways into the Drua setup and will continue their development with the Club as preparations build towards the next campaign.
item.content:encoded:
Explosive backs Joji Nasova and Maika Tuitubou have extended their stay at the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua through to the 2028 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season.

The duo stepped up to the competition level in 2026 after taking different pathways into the Drua setup and will continue their development with the Club as preparations build towards the next campaign.

Nasova made an immediate impression in his first season with the Drua after making the transition from international sevens to Super Rugby Pacific.

The powerful Ba flyer made his Drua and Super Rugby Pacific debut against the Hurricanes at Churchill Park in Lautoka in Round 3 of the 2026 season and has made five appearances for the club ever since.

The powerful outside back also made the step into the Flying Fijians setup before joining the Drua, entering the 2026 season as a capped international with three tests and four tries to his name.

Nasova says he is humbled to be given another opportunity to play in Super Rugby and to wear the Drua jersey again, as well as the feeling of playing in front of family and especially in his hometown of Ba is unbeatable.

Tuitubou says he is looking forward to learning new things with the experienced players and new coaching team.

He also wants to thank his parents for supporting and helping him along the way to achieve his dreams to be a professional rugby player.

The Fijian Drua start their preparation for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season in November.

item.title: Ba banks on home ground advantage to end 8-year BOG title wait
item.description: Dayal's Steel Ba will be looking to make full use of their home ground advantage when they compete in the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants at Four R Stadium at Govind Park. The Fiji Football Association says the Men in Black will have the backing of their home fans as they chase their first BOG title in eight years.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal's Steel Ba will be looking to make full use of their home ground advantage when they compete in the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants at Four R Stadium at Govind Park.

The Fiji Football Association says the Men in Black will have the backing of their home fans as they chase their first BOG title in eight years.

Ba-born coach Ravinesh Kumar will also be aiming to complete a remarkable treble after guiding the side to the 2026 BiC Fiji FACT and Extra Premier League titles since taking charge in May.

Playing at Govind Park will add extra motivation for Ba as they look to lift another major trophy in front of their supporters.

Ba has won the BOG title a record 17 times , as their most recent BOG title came in 2018 when they defeated Suva 2-0 after extra time in the final.

Despite their strong history in the tournament, Ba has gone eight years without lifting the BOG trophy and will be hoping that playing on familiar ground and in front of their home fans can help end the wait.

Ba will face Nadi at 7.30pm on Friday , Rewa at 5.30pm on Saturday and Lautoka at 5.30pm on Sunday in their BOG pool matches.

item.title: Bower to start against Springboks
item.description: George Bower, who has links to Fiji, has been named to start for the All Blacks against the Springboks this Sunday in the second Test of their Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour. Bower joins Codie Taylor and Tyrel Lomax up front, Fabian Holland retains his place in the second row, with Tupou Vai'i moving down from blinside flanker back to locks.
item.content:encoded:
George Bower, who has links to Fiji, has been named to start for the All Blacks against the Springboks this Sunday in the second Test of their Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour.

Bower joins Codie Taylor and Tyrel Lomax up front, Fabian Holland retains his place in the second row, with Tupou Vai'i moving down from blinside flanker back to locks.

Simon Parker joins Luke Jacobson and captain Ardie Savea in the loose trio.

In the backline, the Hurricanes axis of Cam Roigard, Ruben Love and Jordie Barrett will have another opportunity to inflict their will on South Africa, with Quinn Tupaea, Will Jordan and Damian McKenzie completing the team alongside Carter.

On the bench are Asafo Aumua, Zavier Numia, and Fletcher Newell joined by Patrick Tuipulotu, and Peter Lakai as cover for the forwards.

Kyle Preston, Anton Lienert-Brown, and Josh Moorby are cover for the backs.

Coach Dave Rennie says while they were happy with the win last week, he thinks both teams will be better this weekend.

Rennie says they have played four Tests this year and are still growing as a group.

The All Blacks face the Springboks at 3.10am on Sunday.
